lampang.intro: Lampang's best-known tree stands inside Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, the walled hill temple about 18 km south-west of town. It is a khajao, the Indian elm that northern Thailand calls kao jao, listed by the Ministry of Culture as a national heritage tree and as the sacred tree paired with the city. Legend says it grew from a carrying pole pushed into the ground in the Buddha's time. The register is honest that the first tree rotted away and this clump regrew on its spot.
lampang.meta_description: Lampang's heritage khajao at Wat Phra That Lampang Luang: a sacred Indian elm that legend says grew from a carrying pole in the Buddha's time.
lampang.question_meta: Lampang's most famous old tree is the sacred khajao at Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, though its true age is unknown.
lampang.question_answer: Lampang's best-known old tree is the khajao (Indian elm) inside Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, a national heritage tree on the Ministry of Culture's 2018 list. Its legend reaches back to the Buddha's time, but the register says the first tree rotted away and a new clump grew on the same spot, so no honest age can be given for the stems standing today.
lampang.question_context: Thailand's Ministry of Culture began naming heritage trees of the land in 2017, and its 2018 list includes two khajao trees in Lampang under one entry. The one inside Wat Phra That Lampang Luang carries the older story: a Lua man brought honey, coconuts and bael fruit to the Buddha on a pole cut from a khajao, then planted the pole, which took root. People treated the tree as sacred and took pieces of its roots home as amulets. The register does not dress this up. It says the first tree dried and rotted until nothing was left, and that a new one sprouted at the same place as a large clump. So the age column's 'over 1,000 years' cannot honestly be read onto the stems a visitor sees now. The register's other khajao, in Ban Tha Thok in Lampang town, is the one villagers put at more than 1,000 years, but no second source has confirmed it yet. Until someone measures or dates either, Lampang's most famous old tree is famous for its story rather than for a proven age.

faq.q: Where is the sacred khajao tree in Lampang?
faq.a: Inside the grounds of Wat Phra That Lampang Luang in Ko Kha district, about 18 km south-west of Lampang town. The Ministry of Culture's register places it at the temple but not at a spot inside the walls.

faq.q: How old is the khajao at Wat Phra That Lampang Luang?
faq.a: Nobody knows. Its legend dates to the Buddha's time, but the register says the original tree rotted away and a new clump grew on the same spot.
Yes. The temple is free to enter, with donations welcome, and visitor guides give its hours as about 07:30 to 17:00 every day. Cover shoulders and knees.
Khajao, or kao jao in northern Thai, is the Indian elm, Holoptelea integrifolia, a large deciduous tree of South and Southeast Asia.
